title: Contributor command-line bootstrap uses an obsolete SDK path and omits the project toolchain
reproduction: Follow the command-line setup route using the current Android SDK Command-Line Tools layout. The documented tools/bin/sdkmanager path does not exist. Local guarded reproduction from the repository root returned 127 before any SDK manager or build ran. See remaining-tooling-review.md for the exact command and official layout.
expected: Fresh contributors can locate SDK Manager and install/select JDK 21 plus platform android-36, build-tools 36.0.0 and the configured NDK 27.2.12479018 before the existing debug build.
observed: The guide still asks for latest tools and ndk-bundle, calls tools/bin/sdkmanager before defining ANDROID_HOME, does not request platform android-36 or the pinned NDK, and never selects JDK 21. The path failure is directly reproduced; package/JDK omissions are configuration evidence, not a claimed full-build failure.
fix: Replace only the setup paragraph/steps with current Command-Line Tools installation guidance, JAVA_HOME/PATH for JDK 21, ANDROID_HOME before a quoted cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager call, explicit SDK/NDK packages and license review. Retain assembleDebug and the RELEASING.md trust paragraph unchanged.
test_evidence: Read-only shell reproduction: missing executable and exit 127. Parsed command lacks all three pinned package IDs and document lacks JDK 21. Project configuration plus official Android documentation corroborate the correction. SDK/NDK auto-install after license acceptance limits failure claims. Test plan: offline mock of current SDK layout and exact argument/env assertions; separately authorized clean SDK build later. No source/test fix or build performed.
